Settings and performance

In a world, press Esc and choose Settings; on the start menu, choose Settings directly. Most preferences follow you between worlds.

Updated 5 November 2026 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Open the settings

  1. In a world, press Esc and choose Settings. On the start menu, choose Settings directly.
  2. Choose Graphics, Audio, Controls, Gameplay, Interface or Advanced, then a subpage.
  3. Use Find settings or Ctrl+F to search. Enter or Tab leaves the search field; Ctrl+Backspace clears it.
Key or actionWhat it does
Tab / Shift+TabNext / previous group.
Page Up / Page DownPrevious / next subpage; within Key bindings, change action page.
Up / Down arrowsSelect a row or search result.
Left / Right arrows, or EnterChange the selected value.
Click a chip / drag a sliderSet a value directly.
Right-click a rowStep its value backward.
Backspace / Reset pageRestore this page’s defaults, outside text entry. Key bindings resets all keys.

Changes apply immediately. Hover a label for help. Back or Esc returns to the pause menu or start menu; Resume returns to play. Local play pauses; connected servers continue. Settings menu basics

Graphics, controls and interface

  • Graphics > Display > Graphics preset coordinates Shader, Horizon distance, Atmospheric fog, Chunk fade-in and Frame limit. Try Balanced, or Low on a slower computer. Editing a member shows Custom.
  • Shader offers None, Fast (default) or Cinematic. None uses plain lighting; Cinematic adds refined shadows and reflective water at higher GPU cost. Shader quality: None, Fast, Cinematic
  • Horizon distance offers 8, 16, 32, 48, 64 (default), 96, 128, 192, 256, 512 and 1024 chunks. One chunk is 16 m; the largest radius is about 16 km. Nearby detail is separate. Horizon distance
  • Frame limit is 60 (default), 120, 240 or Unlimited. A cap is not a guaranteed frame rate. Frame limit
  • Atmospheric fog is Light, Balanced or Dense. Field of view is 60–96° in 2° steps (default 72°). Chunk fade-in makes newly loaded terrain appear gradually. Atmospheric fog (haze) presets Field of view Chunk fade-in
  • Controls > Mouse has separate horizontal/vertical sensitivity (50–200%) and Invert mouse Y. Use Controls > Key bindings to change gameplay keys; see Controls reference.
  • Gameplay > Movement has Camera bob, Speed FOV, Damage bob and Hold/Toggle choices. Sprint/Sneak default to Hold; Crawl defaults to Toggle.
  • Interface > Layout has GUI presets, custom scale (75–200%), HUD text only, Target info, HUD compass and compact-map heading. Scale is capped so the menu fits. GUI size
  • Interface > Crosshair changes shape (Cross, Dot or Brackets), size, colour and opacity while retaining accuracy feedback.
  • Interface > Accessibility offers high contrast, reduced motion, information-overlay colour palettes and low-survival warnings. Reduce motion suppresses optional bob, FOV kick, shake, fades and pulses.

Sound and music

  • Audio > Volume has separate Master, Music, Effects, Ambience and UI sliders, each 0–100%. Master affects all categories; zero on one category mutes that category alone. Master volume
  • Audio > Music switches music on/off, sets speed from 0.5× to 2.0× in 0.1× steps and offers Previous/Next song. The current title or an audio-unavailable notice appears below. Music: on/off, speed and song choice

Set Ambience to zero to silence nature sounds while keeping effects and music. Nature ambience

Diagnostics

Advanced > Diagnostics has FPS and coordinates, Performance, Chunk borders, LOD view, Voxel view and Distant terrain. The FPS box shows measured frame rate and cap, position in metres and biome. FPS and coordinates readout

Key or actionWhat it does
F3Show or hide the performance overlay. It shows the frame time against your frame budget, the worst recent frame and the CPU work for the last half second.
F7Show or hide chunk borders. The chunk you stand in is gold.
F8Cycle the LOD view: Off, Tint and Colors. Cyan is full detail, and the other colours mark the distant stages.
F9Turn all three diagnostics off, or all on in Tint.
Tip. The keys above are defaults and can be reassigned. The same controls are on Advanced > Diagnostics. Mesh view is labelled unavailable. Chunk borders (F7), LOD view (F8) and all diagnostics (F9) Performance overlay (F3)
  • Voxel view: Off (default), Edges, which tints every block border, or X-ray, which draws only the outlines. Voxel view: block edges and X-ray outlines
  • Distant terrain: on by default. It draws the low-detail horizon beyond the nearby chunks. Turning it off saves work on slow machines. The view then ends at the loaded terrain, and new chunks can appear at that edge when you travel fast. Distant terrain on/off

If the game runs slowly

  1. Try Graphics > Display > Graphics preset > Low: plain shading, 32-chunk horizon, dense fog, no terrain fade and a 60 FPS limit.
  2. If needed, lower Horizon distance further or turn Advanced > Diagnostics > Distant terrain off. The distant view becomes shorter.
  3. Use the default F3 key to compare frame time with the frame budget. Compare the same place/settings before drawing conclusions.

The normal window does not provide live GPU pass timings. This guide has no current hardware benchmark or promised frame-rate gain. Performance overlay (F3)

Which settings follow you

Graphics, audio, interface preferences and key bindings follow the player between worlds. Time, weather and season belong to each world, under Gameplay > World; they are read-only in survival. For profile locations and recovery, see Install, update and find your worlds. World controls and shared preferences

Current limits

Good to know. The 1024-chunk horizon is available as an optional distant view. No current hardware performance result is supplied here. 1024-chunk horizon (about 16 km)
Planned, not in the game. Live GPU pass timings in ordinary play remain planned. The normal window’s GPU box reports unavailable. Live GPU timing in the performance overlay
Good to know. The native app requests that the desktop stay awake while its window is focused and visible, including menus. Desktop support varies; it releases the request on focus loss or hiding. Keep the display awake while playing
